solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pedant and stoic clash violently

indicators.note: a violent clash throws the letters of these words into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy academic and a philosopher of the Stoic school come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a schoolman or narrow academic, a hair-splitting teacher, hence a pedant.

clue.text: Lower class corruptly use bungs

indicators.note: corruptly suggests the letters of use bungs are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Working-class people corruptly use bribes, bungs being British slang for backhanders.
explanation.definitionFit: In taxonomy a subgenus is a rank below genus, a lower biological class.

clue.text: Frost not a great poet

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the a from the combined words

parts.note: hoar is white frost
ace means great, excellent

explanation.surface: Robert Frost was hardly a great poet, someone sniffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' drops one A from HOARACE. Robert Frost, the American poet, makes 'Frost' look like the name it isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was the leading Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: French article put forward case: right to leave union

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

indicators.note: to leave means the right's letter departs from the argue word

parts.note: to argue is to put forward a case

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece argues the case for quitting a union, with a nod to Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance or association, a union of parties.

clue.text: Free programs run, brought in encrypted as we hear

indicators.note: brought in means the run letter is placed among the scrambled ones
encrypted means the letters of as we hear are scrambled as in a code

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Free software is run with encrypted settings, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encrypted' rearranges AS WE HEAR, and 'brought in' puts R inside. 'as we hear' sounds like a homophone hint but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shareware is software distributed freely for trial, often with a request for payment later.

clue.text: Tomb about to be seen by Pound coming into city church

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: coming into means the pound letter enters the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital city of Italy
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A tomb is visited by the poet Ezra Pound arriving at a city church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromlech is a prehistoric stone burial chamber, a megalithic tomb.

clue.text: Sword cutting more flesh from this?

indicators.note: cutting tells us to chop the word more off the sword's name

parts.note: a claymore is a Scottish broadsword

explanation.surface: A swordsman wonders about slicing off more flesh with his blade.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis man is formed from the dust of the ground, often pictured as clay, so mortal flesh is said to be made of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblically and poetically the human body is made of earth, so the material flesh comes from is this substance.

clue.text: Supporting female scientist crossing river from the south

indicators.note: in a down answer, from the south means reading upwards
crossing means the physicist's name spans across the river

parts.note: Paul Dirac was a British theoretical physicist
the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A scientist's female assistant crosses a river from the southern bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts TAY in DIRAC to make DITAYRAC, which 'from the south' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a column carved as a draped woman, a female figure that holds up an entablature.

clue.text: Soul beat wild and perfect

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of soul beat are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frenzied soul rhythm is pronounced flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and total, as in 'an absolute disaster', so utter or perfect.

clue.text: Stop and arrest when finding missionary

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
to nab is to arrest
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Police halt and detain someone when they find a missionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnabas was an early Christian missionary who travelled with Paul in the Acts of the Apostles.

clue.text: Lesser gorgons holding back another fierce woman

indicators.note: back tells us to read the held letters in the opposite direction
the words lesser gorgons hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Minor gorgons keep a second ferocious female at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds SSERGO inside 'leSSER GOrgons', and 'back' turns it round. 'another' works because the gorgons were fierce women too.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre is a monstrous, frightening woman, like the gorgons of myth.

clue.text: Ruled out old notion about daughter having died

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: about means the word for notion goes around the daughter's letter

parts.note: a clue is a notion, as in 'not a clue'
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: An old idea about a daughter's death has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excluded has been ruled out, left out of consideration.

clue.text: Given life, losing heart after temporary release rejected

indicators.note: after places the rejected release in front of the heartless life
rejected tells us to turn the word for temporary release back to front

parts.note: bail is release from custody pending trial

indicators.note: losing heart leaves only the outer letters of the word life

explanation.surface: A prisoner given a life sentence loses heart once bail is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns BAIL into LIAB; 'losing heart' takes IF out of LIFE, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Given to something and inclined to it are synonyms: someone liable to sulk is prone to it.

clue.text: Cold beer first — one Guinness so handled

indicators.note: first puts the beer before the cold

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Pub talk: cold beer first, then a pint of Guinness pulled and handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handled' means named: 'handle' is slang for a name. Sir Alec Guinness was the actor; Guinness is also a stout, which feeds the beer surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Sir Alec Guinness bore this first name, so one Guinness was given this handle.

clue.text: Found pleasure going topless — mad to turn up inside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed madness within the shortened pleasure
going topless means the first letter of the word for pleasure is lost

parts.note: relish is enjoyment or pleasure

indicators.note: in a down answer, turn up means reading the word backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A newly opened topless bar is pleasure gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is the verb to establish, not the past of find. In a down answer 'to turn up' reads upward, and 'going topless' drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, start it from scratch.

clue.text: Man abroad grabbing at politician

indicators.note: grabbing means the foreign man takes hold of the word at inside himself

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a man or gentleman

explanation.surface: A foreign man lunges at a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a legislator and so a politician.

clue.text: Tree forced flat to sprawl among scattered pears

indicators.note: among puts the sprawl word into the midst of the scattered letters
scattered tells us the letters of pears are spread out in another order

parts.note: to lie is to sprawl or lounge

explanation.surface: A pear tree trained flat against a wall sprawls among fallen pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced flat' belongs to the definition: the tree is trained to grow against a wall, and 'scattered' makes ESPAR before 'among' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree trained to grow flat against a wall or trellis.

clue.text: Location of underwater activity miles after sign for docking

indicators.note: after puts the miles letter behind the shortened sign
docking means cutting off the tail, so the last letter of the sign goes

parts.note: Aquarius is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A boat docks miles away, after a signal, with divers at work beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for docking' cuts the tail S off AQUARIUS, and 'after' puts M at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarium is a tank where fish and other creatures go about their business beneath the water.

clue.text: Being church musician, mass preferred to last piece

indicators.note: preferred to the last piece means the mass letter takes the place of the musician's final letter

parts.note: an organist plays the organ in church
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A church organist gives preference to the Mass over the closing voluntary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preferred to last piece' swaps the final T of ORGANIST for M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means a living creature, an individual life form.

clue.text: Shake from second-hand milk dispenser

parts.note: a cow's udder dispenses milk

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a used milk machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-hand' looks like one adjective but splits into its two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder is to shake or tremble convulsively, from fear or disgust.

clue.text: So-called priest has to tear round all the time

indicators.note: round means the tearing word goes around the always word

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
ever means always, all the time

explanation.surface: A priest in name only is always tearing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' is fair because this is the title a priest is called by, not a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the style used for clergy, so a priest is called by this title.

clue.text: Swan for one and others finding peace

definitions.meaning: in snooker the swan is one of the cue supports used for awkward shots

explanation.surface: A swan and other birds find tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a snooker cue support, the remaining ones, and repose.

clue.text: Recovered gambler?

definitions.meaning: well again after an illness, as in 'she is much improved now'
one who bets, a punter; the question mark flags the invented sense

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: improved in health after illness, and a person who places wagers.

clue.text: Sea advanced to claim river and harbour

indicators.note: to claim means the sea and advanced take the river into themselves

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: The sea came forward, swallowing a river and its harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a small harbour for yachts and pleasure boats.

clue.text: Prospect with men vacating isthmus

indicators.note: vacating means the soldiers leave the view

parts.note: a panorama is a wide view or prospect
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A view of an isthmus empties as the men move out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isthmus of Panama is the narrow strip of land joining North and South America.

clue.text: Deny Blunt's smuggled dope from the East

indicators.note: smuggled means the information is slipped inside the word for blunt

parts.note: to abate is to blunt or lessen; the 's reads as 'has'

indicators.note: from the East means the word is read leftwards, from the right

parts.note: gen is slang for information, like dope

explanation.surface: Someone denies that Blunt smuggled in drugs from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Blunt was a Soviet spy, so the capital invites a name; here it is the verb to blunt. In an across answer 'from the East' means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or deny oneself something.

clue.text: British couple from Rome hiding kilo in costume

indicators.note: hiding means the Roman two conceals the other letters inside it

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
K is kilo, as in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A British pair on holiday in Rome hide a kilo of contraband in a swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece bathing costume.

clue.text: Kid held by inspector put away for attack

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: held by means the teasing word sits inside the eating word

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate
to kid and to rib both mean to tease

explanation.surface: A child is detained by a police inspector and locked up for assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack or tirade.

clue.text: Sulphur removed from Salisbury plant

indicators.note: removed from means the sulphur symbol is taken out

parts.note: Sarum is the old name for Salisbury, an English cathedral city
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur has been taken out of a plant in Salisbury, as if a factory had been cleaned up.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum, or cuckoo-pint, is a flowering plant with a hooded spathe.

clue.text: Country seen in alternative light after month

indicators.note: after puts the alternative and the light behind the month

parts.note: other means alternative, as in 'the other option'
to light on something is to land on it, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A country viewed in a different light a month on.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherland is one's native country, the homeland.
